predecessors.name: Free Imperial City of Bremen
predecessors.text: the city of Bremen, a Free Imperial City since 1646

successors.name: Weimar Republic
successors.text: the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (Free Hanseatic City of Bremen)

ledger.x: 1806: the map begins with the Free City of Bremen.
1827: Bremen buys the site of Bremerhaven from Hanover.
November 1918: Bremen, a free city with no monarch, passes from the Empire's member states to a state of the Weimar Republic.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: After the Battle of Leipzig 'the French withdrew' in 1813 and Bremen was restored to its autonomy in the German Confederation.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: No fighting on Bremen land; 'After Prussia defeated Austria in 1866 and annexed Hannover, Bremen joined Berlin in the North German Confederation.'

certainty.note: No page gives Bremen's boundary; the city's land is a scatter of small parcels.
The Bremerhaven strip was bought from Hanover and the free city had fixed frontiers within the German Confederation; the pages record no later change.
